answer: Agents selling ocean tide forecasts or trellis crop advice must earn a key-bound hashcash stamp each epoch: H(beacon, public key, nonce) must have d leading zero bits. Validators check the hash and epoch, rejecting stale or mismatched stamps. An unpredictable beacon prevents precomputation. Each added identity needs about 2^d fresh hash trials. Changing keys invalidates reuse. Thousands of miners can work in parallel, but still pay that expected work per admitted key. This assumes a uniform hash and meaningful energy costs. Efficient hardware retains an advantage.
